KILLED1 · stopped by a stated criterion

KILLED LINKED #latch-pilot-killed Latch as of 2026-11-11 SOURCES DISAGREE

The Latch pilot, a typed-operator admission gate against free chain-of-thought on multi-hop QA, was killed at its preregistered G3 gate: the gated arm scored 37.5% at full coverage against 80.6% for chain-of-thought.

Does not showAnything about gates that anchor to literal artifacts (fetched bytes, export rows). It tests a model translating a free-form question into a formal schema. Scoring was manual and not blinded; few-shot Example 5 was written from errors in the same 72 questions, which makes Arm 2's number optimistic; and PREREG section 5 treats abstentions as 'not answered, never wrong' while the headline scores them as wrong. The kill clause holds under either reading.

Kill criterion
PREREG.md, G3: promote only if Arm 2 beats Arm 0 by >= 15 pp at full coverage with p < 0.05 (McNemar); kill if Arm 2 loses to Arm 0.

The McNemar statistic on the 32 jointly answered questions (b=4, c=2) appears as chi2 = 0.167 in POSTMORTEM.md and the vault, and as chi2 = 0.67, p = 0.41 in paper.tex. Both come from the same cells; the site builder's reading is that one uses a continuity correction, which the author has not confirmed. Neither changes the kill.

Notes
Stage history from POSTMORTEM: G1 promoted (74/100 decomposable; re-annotation 72/100, kappa 0.949). G2 was killed under the strict gate (0% admit), the gate and prompts were redesigned, G2 was killed again on manual review (16 of 26 non-trivial admits structurally valid but semantically wrong), then promoted at about 50% correct formalization with v4 prompts. G3 then killed the pilot.

Built entries with no qualifying measurement in the evidence. Full tags are in the ledger and on project pages.

  • #gin-bookkeeper The Bookkeeper is the single admission gate for GIN's graph state: it checks a confidence floor, endpoint existence, self-loops, anchor integrity, duplicates and DAG acyclicity, then stamps provenance on what it admits.
    Does not showAny measurement of the Bookkeeper. The walk found code and tests, not an eval output for the gate itself. The checks are structural; they do not judge whether an admitted relation is true.
  • #gin-sear-decode-constraint GIN's SEAR layer constrains every generated token, at decode time, to continue a span that occurs verbatim in the retrieved corpus, using a custom llama-cpp-python logits processor.
    Does not showThat the constrained output is correct or fair to its source. Verbatim spans can still be selected or juxtaposed misleadingly. It also does not show behaviour on native Windows: the repo notes the generation path is only exercised under Linux/WSL.
  • #gin-stress-patched Patches to retrieval, the relation detector and federation, written against those failures, raised the same benchmark's scores: relation detector F1 0.686 to 0.982, production peer selection 0.488 to 0.872, retrieval top-1 0.914 to 1.000, stopword-trap refusal 4 of 5 to 5 of 5.
    Does not showThat the fixes generalize. They were written after seeing failures on this exact set and re-scored on it, so these are fit scores, not held-out scores. One patch adds the exact units the set tests (euro, pound, km/h, GW, hectares). Issue-framing recall stayed at 0 of 15.
  • #sear-demo-pipeline sear-demo is a corpus-grounded answer pipeline with a verification gate: the model writes freely, then each claim must be entailed by its cited chunk (NLI) and every name and number must appear in it, or the claim is dropped; an explicit failure state replaces guessing.
    Does not showDecode-time constraint: this is SEAR's verify-after stage, not GIN's decode-time mask. Verified is not true: the gate enforces the corpus, not the world (see sear-poisoned-fork).
  • #sear-demo-results On its 27-probe main set, sear-demo refused all 9 probes that should be refused, but 5 of its 14 failure states were on probes that had a supportable answer.
    Does not showA measurement. The README says every number is a smoke test, not a measurement (13 chunks, 27 + 6 + 5 probes). Retrieval is not tested: top_k 12 of 13 chunks means the generator sees almost the whole corpus.
